102.title: Self Publishing Runtime Protocol (SPRP) — ทุก Runtime Component ต้องรับผิดชอบการประกาศการมีอยู่ของตัวเอง (identity/capability/state/health/dependency/resource/owner/execution-status/improvement-request) เชิงรุก ห้ามให้ AI ค้นพบด้วยการไล่อ่าน source code (CONST-102, DNA-000031)
enforced_by: core/shared/types.ts (RuntimeContract 19-field type, NegotiationFlowState, computeNegotiationStage — SDRN-P6, DNA-000060)
plugins/drivers/line.selfDescription.ts (getLineDriverRuntimeContract — full 19-field real implementation, 2nd real module)
core/shared/types.ts (ContextBudget, DeltaContext, WorkOrder, ExecutionReadiness, VerificationContract, MeasurementReport + real derivation functions — SDRN-P7, DNA-000061)
core/runtime/contextBroker.ts (SDRN-P8, DNA-000062 — real compute-once/cache/reuse broker, real read counter)

102.detection: NOT mechanical. Recorded honestly as a declared engineering target, not an enforced rule. Real coverage today: engines/documents/selfDescription.ts implements the 'describe on demand' half of this (SelfDescribe(), SDRN-P1) for exactly 1 of 466 modules; scripts/hello.ts is the one real place anything gets composed/published, and only on manual invocation (npm run hello), not proactively/continuously. The Publish*() interface family (PublishState/PublishHealth/PublishNeed/PublishDependency/PublishCapability/PublishKnowledge/PublishWarning/PublishProposal), inter-component negotiation, and continuous self-reporting do not exist anywhere in this codebase. The closest existing prior art — per Rule 101, checked before writing this entry rather than assumed — is core/workspace/runtimeRegistry.ts (register/unregister/getStatus/list/subscribe, a real pub/sub-shaped primitive already built for the Visual Workspace canvas), but register() is called nowhere in the app (confirmed multiple times this session) and it only covers state, not the other 8 Publish* categories. Building SPRP for real would mean extending that existing primitive, not creating a second one — and is Feature-scale work requiring its own Plan Lock exception and phased scope, same as SDRN-P1/P2, not something this rule entry itself performs. UPDATE (DNA-000059): the real implementation (engines/documents/selfDescription.ts) now covers all 9 C-011 fields — added `constraints` and `verificationProcedure` (previously absent from core/shared/types.ts's SelfDescription interface entirely) plus `missingKnowledge` (distinct from the pre-existing `missing`), verified live via a direct tsx invocation returning real, non-fabricated values for all 3. Still true: only 1 of ~470 registered modules has any SelfDescription implementation at all — this closes a field-completeness gap for that one module, it does not extend coverage to more modules. UPDATE (DNA-000060, SDRN-P6): the full 19-field RuntimeContract (Identity/Purpose/Responsibilities/Capabilities/Dependencies/Constraints/Health/Current State/Known Problems/Missing Knowledge/Missing Capabilities/Missing Dependencies/Resources Needed/Requested Actions/Execution Scope/Forbidden Scope/Verification Procedure/Success Criteria/Confidence/Last Validation) plus a real, pure computeNegotiationStage() function now exist as real types/code — verified live via direct tsx invocation for 2 real modules (Document Engine, LINE driver), both returning genuinely computed (not fabricated) values, including a correctly-computed 'knowledge_gap' negotiation stage for both (Document Engine: unwired Capability Orchestrator chain + no versioning scheme; LINE driver: no automated functional test for the AppleScript automation). Still true: only 2 of ~470 registered modules have any RuntimeContract implementation — this was an explicit, scoped Plan Lock exception (SDRN-P6), not a repo-wide rollout, and the owner's stated end-goal (contract-first replacing repository-first discovery for all future AI sessions) remains a declared target, not something now mechanically enforced for AI behavior in general. UPDATE (DNA-000061, SDRN-P7): real Contract Coverage measured live — 2 of 473 registered modules (0.42%). The other 6 named metrics (Repository Read Count, Context Size, Context Reuse Ratio, Delta Context Ratio, Repository Scan Avoidance, Execution Preparation Time) are real TYPES with honest null values and a stated unmeasurableReason — this repository has no access to AI session token/read/timing data, which lives in the Claude Code harness outside this repo. Per the owner's own explicit instruction, no numeric reduction is claimed. ExecutionReadiness/ContextBudget/DeltaContext/WorkOrder are real, computed, and verified live for the same 2 modules — explicitly advisory only, nothing mechanically gates AI execution on these values. UPDATE (DNA-000062, SDRN-P8): real before/after measurement now exists and was run live — 55 real repository reads (independent recomputation) vs 11 real repository reads (broker, cached) for the same 2-module repeated-access workload, an 80% real, computed reduction (not estimated). Precisely scoped: this measures the broker's own internal behavior only, not an AI session's overall token/read behavior, which remains outside this repository's observability. UPDATE (DNA-000063, SDRN-P9): after auditing a 10-item 'Runtime Knowledge Platform' directive against real state (3 items already built, 1 overlapping knip/jscpd, several not achievable — mechanical repository-access gating and AI-reasoning caching are not data this repo can observe or store), the owner confirmed a narrowed scope. ExecutionPlan/ExecutionReport built and verified live for both real modules across a real cache-miss and cache-hit — repositoryReads correctly stayed flat and executionTimeMs correctly dropped to 0 on the cache hit, confirming real, not fabricated, behavior. UPDATE (DNA-000064, SDRN-P10): RuntimePacket now includes briefing (real synthesis) and architecture (real module-registry.json/dependency-graph.json lookup). A real bug was caught and fixed live in this same pass — architecture's first implementation added real file reads even on a cache hit, contradicting the already-verified 0-additional-reads claim; fixed by caching it alongside the contract, re-verified (8 reads unchanged across a cache-hit access).
102.canonical_id: C-011 (Every module must be self-describing; no AI may inspect implementation before reading self-description)

103.title: Reuse Before Build — ก่อนสร้าง module/registry/runtime/database/API/workflow/event bus/cache/service/interface/storage ใหม่ใด ๆ ต้องค้นหาก่อนว่ามี implementation เดิมอยู่แล้วหรือไม่ ทุก request ต้องได้ข้อสรุปเป็นหนึ่งใน 3: EXISTING (ใช้ของเดิม) / EXTEND (ต่อยอดของเดิม) / NEW (สร้างใหม่ เฉพาะเมื่อพิสูจน์แล้วว่าไม่มีของเดิมที่ใช้ได้) ทุกบรรทัดโค้ดใหม่ต้องอธิบายได้ว่าทำไมโค้ดเดิมแก้ปัญหานี้ไม่ได้ (CONST-103, DNA-000036)
103.detection: Mechanical only at the same narrow layer Rule 101 already covers — module/file-basename duplication (Guard 9, confirmed_duplicate_pairs). The EXISTING/EXTEND/NEW decision framework itself has no mechanical check — nothing in this codebase can algorithmically determine whether a proposed capability semantically overlaps 80%+ with an existing one; that judgment is currently made by whoever is building (human or AI) actually searching first. Real, lived evidence this rule already describes existing practice rather than inventing new behavior: every SDRN-P1 through P5 phase this session applied exactly this EXISTING/EXTEND/NEW test before writing code (e.g. SDRN-P3 found core/workspace/runtimeRegistry.ts already existed and extended it instead of building a second registry; SDRN-P5 built on engines/documents/selfDescription.ts instead of a new interface file; the persistence-model decision was deferred rather than building a new event bus without evidence one was needed). Not claiming this makes the discipline automatic — it documents that it has been followed manually, consistently, and gives it a rule number so future sessions (human or AI) are held to the same standard explicitly rather than by accumulated precedent alone.

104.title: Nothing Is Wasted — ก่อนลบ source code ใด ๆ ต้อง extract ความรู้ก่อนเสมอ (purpose/owner/dependencies/failure reason/replacement/migration path/lessons learned) ทุก implementation ที่ retire แล้วต้องกลายเป็น Runtime Knowledge (registry/existence.json) และห้ามสร้าง implementation ใหม่ที่ recreate mistake ที่เคย archive ไว้ — ทุกการ REJECT ต้องอ้างอิง knowledge จริงที่เป็นเหตุผล ไม่ใช่แค่ชี้ไปที่ไฟล์เฉย ๆ (CONST-104, DNA-000037/038/039/040)

(2) Guard 10 (pre-commit-check.sh) hard-REJECTs if a new file recreates the basename of an already-archived module, AND its rejection message resolves and prints the real matched archived_knowledge entry's id/failure_reason/replacement_successor directly — not just a generic pointer at the file (DNA-000040, verified by copying an archived file to a new path and confirming the printed AK-001 id, real failure_reason text, and real replacement_successor path). Deliberately excludes conventional/repeated-by-design basenames (index.ts, engine.ts, etc., same list Guard 9 already excludes) — 2 of the 4 currently-archived files (engines/impact/engine.ts, core/auth/index.ts) have exactly this basename-genericity problem and were excluded after a dry run proved they'd otherwise hard-reject the repo's own real, unrelated files (10+ real engine.ts, 30+ real index.ts). 105.title: Autonomous Architecture Maintenance Authorization — Runtime/AI may modify without re-asking approval when all 4 conditions hold (existing-rules-compliant, no business-logic change, scope limited to maintenance/sync/repair/metadata/dependency-correction/docs/validation/tooling, passes all validators before+after); every autonomous change must record executor/timestamp/affected modules-files-functions/reason/root cause/validation before-after/rollback into CHANGELOG.json + VALIDATION_RESULTS.json + CURRENT_STATE.json; exceeding Constitution scope means stop and create an Owner Task instead (CONST-105, DNA-000052)

NOT mechanical: whether a proposed change actually qualifies under the 4 conditions (especially condition 2, "does not change Business Logic") is judged by the executing AI itself — no guard inspects a diff and rejects it for being out of the autonomous-maintenance scope before it happens.
